turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Mrs Iyer, before you go in. Weight today is seventy-nine kilograms. Blood pressure is one thirty-six over eighty-four, pulse seventy-two.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Seventy-nine? At my daughter's house the scale said seventy-two only. This saree is heavy, and I had idli and coffee, so maybe that is sitting on me.
[SEG0003] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Shoes were off, ma'am. This is our scale. Doctor is free, please go in.
[SEG0004] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sit. What is it?
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): Right knee, doctor. It is paining when I go down the stairs. Sharp, catching type of pain.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): Coming up the stairs?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Up I can manage. Down is the real problem. At night also, if I turn in the bed it wakes me, and the fan was rattling so I thought the noise was from the knee, silly—
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): How long has it been?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): How long, see, after Diwali we went to my sister in Pune, and their staircase is so narrow I was holding the wall the whole—
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): About four months. The stair pain and the night pain, both, from around that time.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): On the flat road?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Short distance is alright. I still go down for the milk, three floors, no lift in the building. Morning and evening, every day, what to do.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): Swelling?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Swelling, no. My neighbour Mrs Deshpande, her knee came up like a drum and they rushed her—
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): Your knee. Swollen, yes or no?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Not swollen.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): Does it lock, or give way?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No locking. It does not give way also.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any redness? Fever?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No redness, no fever. I am cooking and moving about, only this pain.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): What are you taking for it?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Diclofenac gel, the one percent, morning and night, I rub it on the right knee. From the pharmacy. Sometimes the diclofenac tablets also, when the pain is too much.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): What strength are the tablets, and how often?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): The pharmacy fellow near the Ganesh temple just hands me the strip, I did not even look at the—
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): I think fifty milligram. Two or three times in a week, not daily, only when it is bad.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any stomach trouble from them?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No stomach problem. I take curd rice at night, and I have left off the pickle in this heat, so the stomach is—
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any burning?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Actually, yes, there is heartburn. A burning after I take the tablet, mostly in the evening. I was not counting that as a stomach problem.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Stop the tablets. Keep the gel, morning and night.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Gel only, then. It helps for a few hours and then the pain sneaks back. My daughter says at sixty-seven I should not be swallowing pain tablets, she phones every Sunday—

[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sixty-seven, with seventy-nine kilos on the knee. Downstairs pain and night pain can be osteoarthritis, wear and tear, or a cartilage niggle. I am not concluding which one, not today.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Wear and tear, yes. My sister in Chennai got the full knee changed, she was on a walker for weeks, and the hospital food—
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): No surgery talk. Physiotherapy is one option, or an injection into the knee. I am not booking either.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Needles I don't like. Physio is two buses away, though last time for my shoulder the girl was very patient with the band exercises—
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): We choose next time. Come in four weeks. Meanwhile lose two or three kilos if you can, walk on the flat, and take the stairs one at a time.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Two kilos I will try, less rice at night. The milk boy has quit, so I still climb those three floors, and that itself is exercise, no?
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hold the rail. Pain in the other knee, or anywhere else?
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Left knee is fine. Shoulders and hands are okay. Only this right one.
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): No diclofenac by mouth. Gel as before. If the knee swells suddenly or you cannot put weight on it, come before the four weeks.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): If it swells, I come early. The heartburn should go once I stop the tablets, isn't it?
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): It ought to settle. If the burning is still there next time we will look. No stomach tablet from me today.
[SEG0043] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Sorry, doctor. Next patient is waiting. Shall I book Mrs Iyer in four weeks, morning?
[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes. Four weeks, morning.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): Morning only, please. Afternoons are the temple committee, the lamp festival, and they want jasmine from my garden—
[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): Morning. That is all.
[SEG0047] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Booked, ma'am. Four weeks, morning clinic. I will put it on your card.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you both. I will keep the gel, stop the tablets, and take a little less rice. We will see how the knee goes.
